symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Number of untreated pre-event calendar windows.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Last return horizon in one buy-and-hold block.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Number of proxy coordinates at each return horizon.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: The event date is \(t=0\); dates \(t\ge1\) index untreated pseudo-event windows.

symbols.name: n_s
symbols.def: Number of replicated units in cohort \(s\) at every calendar window.

symbols.name: a_minus
symbols.def: \(\mathbf a_{-si}\), the assignments of units other than \(i\) in cohort \(s\).

symbols.name: ell

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.def: Holder smoothness of each historical conditional-mean surface.

symbols.name: E_0

symbols.name: Delta_DID

symbols.name: B_si_a

symbols.name: X_st

symbols.name: Q_sti_a
symbols.def: Potential pseudo-event terminal wealth under event-path status \(a\).

symbols.name: Q_sti

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Law of the event state, donor sample, exact historical paths, replicated pseudo-event outcomes, and event outcomes.

symbols.name: P_0
symbols.def: First law in a channelwise two-point experiment.

symbols.name: P_1
symbols.def: Second law in a channelwise two-point experiment.

symbols.name: P_lq

symbols.name: beta_P

symbols.name: Z_plus

symbols.name: tau_n
symbols.def: Cohort-weighted finite-population average event effect on terminal level wealth.

symbols.name: omega_P
symbols.def: Covariance-standardized local change of the weighted untreated surface.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Bounded compactly supported product kernel of order \(r\).

symbols.name: b_r
symbols.def: Vector of monomials in \(u\in\mathbb R^d\) with total degree at most \(r\).

symbols.name: hat_Sigma

symbols.name: hat_m_s

symbols.name: hat_tau
symbols.def: Cross-fitted cohort-weighted event average minus the raw fitted untreated mean.

symbols.name: theta_FWL
symbols.def: Cohort-weighted event-dummy coefficient after partialing out cohort-specific local-polynomial columns.

symbols.name: R_q
symbols.def: \(R_q\) equals the rate component indexed by \(q\).

symbols.name: tilde_z_sk

symbols.name: h_sk

symbols.name: hat_theta_sk
symbols.def: Event coefficient from the foldwise algebraic weighted least-squares problem.

symbols.name: hat_gamma_sk
symbols.def: Polynomial coefficient from the foldwise algebraic weighted least-squares problem.

symbols.name: O_mean
symbols.def: Collection of the initial-wealth law, coordinatewise conditional return means, and treated terminal-wealth mean.

symbols.name: a_w

symbols.name: rho_fun
symbols.def: Conditional sign-correlation surface in the mean-only witness.

symbols.name: rho_class

symbols.name: V_si

symbols.name: V_sti

symbols.name: hat_tau_R_minus_b

symbols.name: m_k

symbols.name: C_alpha

novel.justification: This cohort-average cross-date path-law stability condition is plausible for short event windows whose untreated wealth mechanism is stable after conditioning on the realized market path; rolling pseudo-events make its pre-event analogue diagnostically accessible without requiring event-date exchangeability.
Finite-horizon wealth is naturally bounded after the same pre-specified return filters or winsorization rules used to protect long-horizon event studies from single-security price errors.
Finite-horizon wealth is naturally bounded after the same pre-specified return filters or winsorization rules used to protect long-horizon event studies from single-security price errors.
Separate donor universes or pre-registered sample splitting produce this conditional independence while retaining the same realized market event state.
Administrative panels record the historical proxy coordinates used to index pseudo-event windows, so classical measurement error is absent from the training design.

The condition holds for regular surfaces with a nonzero covariance-standardized gradient when \(\lambda>1\), and for asymmetric Holder cusps with a coefficient bounded away from zero when \(0<\lambda\le1\); both describe economically meaningful path sensitivity rather than an oracle estimator property.
A positive-probability interior event-state region is natural when market states have a density and prevents a conditional lower bound from resting on a null query.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)=\{P_{N,T,(n_s)_{s=1}^{S}}:\text{ each indexed joint panel law satisfies }\texttt{ass:consistency}\text{ through }\texttt{ass:positive-query-region}\}\).

definitions.name: Generated-center replicated local-polynomial estimator
definitions.construction: Split \((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\) into \(K_D\) folds. For fold \(k\), project the complementary donor mean onto \(([0,1]^d)^S\) and denote cohort \(s\)'s block by \(\widetilde z_{sk}\). Select \(h_{sk}\) as the first bandwidth on a finite dyadic grid above \(h_s\) whose historical polynomial Gram matrix has minimum eigenvalue at least a fixed fraction of \(c_X\). On a successful fit set \(u_{stk}=(X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk})/h_{sk}\), \(w_{stk}=K(u_{stk})\), and let \(\widehat\gamma_{sk}\) minimize \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stk}[Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{stk})^{\top}\gamma]^2\). Define the raw fold-averaged fit \(\widehat m_s=K_D^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}e_0^{\top}\widehat\gamma_{sk}\) and \(\widehat\tau=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s)\). On a failed selected fit set its intercept contribution to zero. Estimate \(\Sigma\) by the spectrally clipped full sample covariance \(\widehat\Sigma\); no clipping is applied to a successful fitted intercept or to \(\widehat\tau\).

definitions.name: Algebraic foldwise weighted least-squares panel regression
definitions.construction: For each \((s,k)\), set \(u_{stk}=(X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk})/h_{sk}\), \(w_{stk}=K(u_{stk})\), and \(e_0=b_r(0)\). On a successful selected fit define \((\widehat\theta_{sk},\widehat\gamma_{sk})\) as a minimizer of \[\frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\theta-e_0^{\top}\gamma]^2+\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stk}[Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{stk})^{\top}\gamma]^2.\] Equivalently, use one block-diagonal stacked regression: event rows have \(D=1\), polynomial row \(e_0\), and weight \(1/n_s\); historical rows have \(D=0\), polynomial row \(b_r(u_{stk})\), and weight \(w_{stk}\); outer block weights are \(\pi_s/K_D\). Define \(\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sK_D^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}\widehat\theta_{sk}\).

definitions.name: Total full-covariance calendar-block interval
definitions.construction: Fix \(\alpha_{\mathrm{tr}}=\alpha_{\mathrm{cal}}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha/3\), \(g_T=\lceil3\log(T\vee2)/|\log\rho_0|\rceil\), \(\ell_T=\lceil T^{1/3}\rceil\), and \(M=\lfloor T/(\ell_T+g_T)\rfloor\). Form consecutive retained blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_M\) of length \(\ell_T\), separated by discarded gaps of length \(g_T\), and let \(R_T=\bigcup_{b=1}^{M}I_b\). Apply exactly the donor folds, projected complementary-fold centers, bandwidth grid and selection rule, and raw local-polynomial intercepts of \texttt{def:feasible-estimator} using only historical rows in \(R_T\); call the result \(\widehat\tau_R\). For every \(b\), rerun this retained-data construction after deleting \(I_b\), without reassigning donor folds or changing the bandwidth grid, and call it \(\widehat\tau_R^{(-b)}\). On successful fits set \(G_{sk}^{R}=\sum_{t\in R_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stk}b_r(u_{stk})b_r(u_{stk})^{\top}\), \(a_{stik}^{R}=e_0^{\top}(G_{sk}^{R})^{-1}w_{stk}b_r(u_{stk})\), and thus \(e_0^{\top}\widehat\gamma_{sk}^{R}=\sum_{t\in R_T}\sum_i a_{stik}^{R}Q_{sti}\). Define \[A_L=C_{r,d}L\sum_{s=1}^{S}(\pi_s/K_D)\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}\sum_{t\in R_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{stik}^{R}|\,\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^{\lambda}.\] Define \(J_b=M\widehat\tau_R-(M-1)\widehat\tau_R^{(-b)}\), \(\bar J=M^{-1}\sum_bJ_b\), \(C_b=J_b-\bar J\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{cal}}=\{M(M-1)\}^{-1}\sum_bC_b^2\). Define \(E_{si}=(\pi_s/n_s)(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}})\), \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_s\sum_iE_{si}^2\), and report \(\widehat V=\widehat V_{\mathrm{cal}}+\widehat V_{\mathrm{tr}}\). Conditional on the data, draw mutually independent Rademacher variables \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_M\) and \(\eta_{si}\), and set \(G_{\mathrm{cal}}^{\#}=\{M(M-1)\}^{-1/2}\sum_b\xi_bC_b\) and \(G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}=\sum_s\sum_i\eta_{si}E_{si}\). With the exact conditional Rademacher law and randomized tie-breaking when needed, set \(r_{\mathrm{cal}}=\inf\{r:P_{\#}(|G_{\mathrm{cal}}^{\#}|\le r)\ge1-\alpha_{\mathrm{cal}}\}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=\inf\{r:P_{\#}(|G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}|\le r)\ge1-\alpha_{\mathrm{tr}}\}\); a finite zero empirical variance gives radius zero. For donor fold \(k\) with complementary size \(m_k\), put \(D=Sd\), \(Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\), \(M_4(m_k)=B/m_k+(1-1/m_k)(D^2+2D)\), \(q_k=\{K_DM_4(m_k)/\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\}^{1/4}\), \(\delta_k=\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,q_k/\sqrt{m_k}\), and \(A_{\mathrm{don}}=(C_{\mathrm{mod}}/K_D)\sum_k\delta_k^\kappa\). The factor \(\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\) accounts for Euclidean projection onto \(([0,1]^d)^S\) and conversion back to the full-\(\Sigma\) norm. The feasible \(\widehat\Sigma\) remains the spectrally clipped covariance estimate, while the uniform donor radius uses only the known class constants. On the good sample set \(H_\alpha=r_{\mathrm{cal}}+r_{\mathrm{tr}}+A_L+A_{\mathrm{don}}\) and \(C_\alpha=[-B,B]\cap[\widehat\tau_R-H_\alpha,\widehat\tau_R+H_\alpha]\). The bad-sample event is the union of \(M<3\); some \(m_k<1\); failure of any full-sample or delete-one-block selected Gram matrix at its declared eigenvalue threshold; nonfiniteness of a required fit, pseudo-score, variance, or conditional multiplier quantile; undefined spectral clipping; and \(\max_k\delta_k>\delta_0\). On this event set \(C_\alpha=[-B,B]\).

definitions.name: Mean-only return-path information map
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P)=\{\mathcal L_P(W_{si,-1}\mid E_0),\ (x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[R_{sih}(a)\mid X=x,E_0])_{s,h,a},\ \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]\}\).

definitions.name: Correlated-sign mean-only witness
definitions.construction: Set \(S=1\), \(H=1\), \(W_{1i,-1}=1\), and fix \(0<a_{\mathrm w}<1\). For \(\rho\in\mathcal R\), define the event and historical sign pairs by \[P_\rho(U_{1i}=u,V_{1i}=v\mid z_{01}=x,E_0)=P_\rho(U_{1ti}=u,V_{1ti}=v\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)=\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4},\qquad u,v\in\{-1,1\}.\] Set \(R_{1i0}(0)=a_{\mathrm w}U_{1i}\), \(R_{1i1}(0)=a_{\mathrm w}V_{1i}\), and \(R_{1ih}(1)=0\), so \(B_{1i}(1)=1\). At each historical window use conditionally independent sign-pair copies across units and set \(Q_{1ti}=(1+a_{\mathrm w}U_{1ti})(1+a_{\mathrm w}V_{1ti})\). Complete the remaining panel and donor variables independently within the maintained envelopes, with an i.i.d. calendar process and nondegenerate conditional response variance.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\), \[\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}.\] On every realized sample for which all selected Gram matrices pass and the foldwise minimizers exist, profiling the event coefficient gives \(\widehat\theta_{sk}=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^{\top}\widehat\gamma_{sk}\); the event term then has no \(\gamma\)-dependent component, the fitted \(\widehat\gamma_{sk}\) is exactly the historical local-polynomial fit in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}, and \(\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}=\widehat\tau\) exactly.
statements.justification: This result ties the statistical regression target to a causal level-wealth estimand and to an implementable panel coefficient.
statements.gap: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu identify linear return effects under factor stability; the displayed functional instead identifies compounded level wealth through a path-conditioned nonparametric transport relation.
statements.consumer: Applied financial event studies obtain a declared coefficient and estimand rather than treating a generated synthetic path as an informal benchmark.

statements.statement: The construction in \texttt{def:mean-only-witness} embeds a relatively open family \(\{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}\subset\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\). For every admissible \(\rho\) and \(x\), the untreated return-coordinate means are zero and their conditional coordinate marginals are identical across \(\rho\), whereas \[m_1^{P_\rho}(x)=\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]=1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(x),\qquad \tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)=-a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(z_0).\] Hence there are interior \(\rho_0,\rho_1\in\mathcal R\) with \(\rho_0(z_0)\ne\rho_1(z_0)\) such that \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho_0})=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho_1})\), and their conditional return-coordinate marginals are also identical, but \[|\tau_{n,P_{\rho_1}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{\rho_0}}(z_0)|=a_{\mathrm w}^2|\rho_1(z_0)-\rho_0(z_0)|>0.\] Therefore \(\tau_n\) is not a functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\). This conclusion concerns only mean-only return-path matching; the full historical wealth panel may distinguish the two laws.
statements.justification: The result isolates the information loss from discarding within-path dependence without denying identification from the maintained full wealth panel.
statements.gap: Barber--Lyon and Goldsmith-Pinkham--Lyu diagnose volatility drag; this proposition gives an explicit two-law, relatively open nonidentification result for the restricted mean-only map while preserving full-panel identification under event transport.
statements.consumer: Analysts can determine whether a return-matching procedure discards dependence information needed for a finite-cohort compounded-wealth effect.

statements.statement: For each of the treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, random-spacing, and covariance-aligned donor channels, there are pairs \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\subset\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\) with \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\) such that \(P_{\ell,q}(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\mid E_0)\ge c_X\), the joint observed-data Kullback--Leibler divergence is bounded by a universal constant, and \(|\tau_{n,P_{1,q}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,q}}(z_0)|^2\ge cR_q\) on \(\mathcal Z_+\). Every pair is induced by a regular conditional law of the complete causal panel rather than by a labeled fixed-query kernel.
statements.justification: This is the missing bridge from conditional statistical experiments to an admissible causal panel converse.
statements.gap: The banked predecessor supplied only labeled fixed-query witnesses and no panel-induced lower bound.
statements.consumer: The sharp frontier can be cited as a result about causal panels rather than only about an auxiliary regression experiment.

statements.statement: There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on fixed class constants, such that along every array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), uniformly for \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\) and \(P\)-almost every \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\), \[cR_\star\le\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]\le CR_\star.\] The raw feasible estimator in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator} attains the upper bound with nonidentically distributed bounded event outcomes, an unknown heteroskedastic donor law, and estimated full \(\Sigma\).
statements.justification: The theorem closes the joint-panel upper-and-lower frontier across arbitrary relative growth rates.
statements.gap: Yan, Yao, and Zhou cover repeated-measurement prediction and Akhavan--Gogolashvili--Tsybakov cover an estimated strongly convex minimizer; neither has a causal joint law, a first-order external center, or a realized spacing barrier.
statements.consumer: Empirical designers can determine whether adding donor securities, calendar windows, or cohort replications is the only way to reduce causal wealth risk.

statements.statement: Uniformly over fixed \(S\), \[R_{\mathrm{sm}}\le C\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\},\qquad R_\star\asymp R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.\] The oracle region is \(N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})\), the generated-proxy region is \(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}=o(N^{-\kappa})\), and the boundary is \(N\asymp(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})^{-1/\kappa}\). Exact historical coordinates imply that neither a deconvolution exponent nor a separate moving-Gram phase occurs, and \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\) for every \(\lambda>1\).
statements.justification: The exact diagram distinguishes a genuinely active information channel from a bookkeeping term and records higher-order saturation.
statements.gap: The repeated-measurement literature has a sparse-to-dense smoothing transition, while generated-regressor and measurement-error papers imply different first-stage effects; no existing result locates this oracle boundary.
statements.consumer: A study can allocate its data budget to the active axis and avoid unnecessary deconvolution when the historical paths are exact.

statements.statement: The total interval \(C_\alpha\) in \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies \[\liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)}P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\ge1-\alpha,\qquad\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]\le CR_\star^{1/2}.\] Every interval with the same uniform conditional coverage has worst-case conditional expected length at least \(cR_\star^{1/2}\). The retained-block coupling error obeys \(M\beta_0\rho_0^{g_T}=o(1)\); the block jackknife/Rademacher law consistently estimates the calendar fluctuation; and the event Rademacher law handles the bounded, conditionally independent, nonidentically distributed finite-cohort summands. Under the donor replication and covariance assumptions, the \(Y_j\) are independent with \(\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^{\top}\mid E_0]=I_D\), and \(\mathbb E_P[\|m_k^{-1/2}\sum_{j\notin k}Y_j\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le M_4(m_k)\) implies \(P\{\max_k\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\operatorname{vec}((\widetilde z_{sk})_{s=1}^{S})-z_0)\|_2>\delta_k\mid E_0\}\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\) by Markov's inequality and a union bound. Separate calibration of the calendar and event components introduces no event/history independence assumption, and Bonferroni over the three error allocations gives coverage. Discarded gaps are \(o(T)\), \(M\to\infty\), selected-Gram failures have vanishing probability at the required order, \(A_L=O_P((R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})^{1/2})\), \(A_{\mathrm{don}}=O(N^{-\kappa/2})\), and \(r_{\mathrm{cal}}+r_{\mathrm{tr}}=O_P((R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})^{1/2}+R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2})\). The bounds therefore hold for every relative growth regime without undersmoothing, an extra deconvolution term, or a multiplicative logarithmic phase.
statements.justification: Risk optimality alone does not guarantee honest conditional uncertainty quantification at phase boundaries.
statements.gap: Armstrong--Kolesar use a fixed Gaussian operator and Cattaneo--Feng--Titiunik treat constrained linear prediction; neither establishes expected-length optimality for this moving-center product experiment.
statements.consumer: Event-study confidence intervals remain valid when calendar overlap, donor covariance estimation, and nonparametric bias are simultaneously first order.

statements.statement: If \(H=0\), \(S=1\), the proxy is the baseline outcome, and \(m_1(x)=x+\Delta_0\) with \(\Delta_0\) equal to the untreated two-period cohort-average mean change, then the functional in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} equals the canonical finite-cohort two-period difference-in-differences estimand. If treatment effects are homogeneous across cohorts and there is no carry-over beyond \(h=0\), then \(\tau_n(z_0)\) reduces to the common contemporaneous finite-cohort average treatment effect on level wealth.
statements.justification: Named reductions anchor the new compounded-path object to familiar panel estimands.
statements.gap: The banked predecessor did not provide a canonical DID or homogeneous-panel reduction.
statements.consumer: Readers can audit the identifying functional against a standard two-period benchmark before using the general event-path result.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on the observed event state \(E_0\), each cohort contributes \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with a density bounded above and away from zero; their calendar sequence is geometrically beta mixing.
sampling_model.units: At each pre-event path, cohort \(s\) supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded untreated wealth blocks, and the event date supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded treated wealth levels; event units need not be identically distributed.
sampling_model.treatment: The event occurs at \(t=0\). Consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and the maintained cross-date cohort-average event-transport equality identify the untreated finite-cohort event mean from the historical path regression.
sampling_model.overlap: The realized event path lies in an interior positive-probability region and every historical design density is bounded below there.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query and its unknown full heteroskedastic covariance. Historical training coordinates are exact. Fold-specific projected donor means, covariance spectral clipping, retained calendar blocks with fixed gaps, delete-block refits, separate exact Rademacher calibrations for calendar and event fluctuations, and a fourth-moment donor radius yield a total feasible procedure.

estimand_functional: \(\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\), estimated by the raw \(\widehat\tau\) with \(\sup_P\operatorname{MSE}(\widehat\tau\mid E_0)\asymp R_\star\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper derives identification and asymptotic-bias conditions for financial event-study estimators and explains that buy-and-hold comparisons require volatility matching.
The Holder repeated-measurement prediction rate has sparse order \((nm)^{-2s/(2s+d)}\) and dense order \(n^{-1}\), up to the stated logarithmic qualifications.
A local-polynomial Lepski procedure adapts pointwise to local design mass and local Holder smoothness under observed random design.
Theorem 1 expands local-linear regression with a generated covariate attached to every training observation through smoothed first-stage errors.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 establish deconvolution rates when latent training coordinates have replicated classical measurement error.
Theorems 7--8 evaluate a rate-optimal local-polynomial regression estimator at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer.
The dependent-data theorem uses large-block--small-block coupling for conditional approximation of synthetic-control prediction error.
Spline and wavelet series estimators attain optimal uniform rates and functional normality under beta mixing and weak moments.
Ordered moduli characterize optimal confidence procedures for linear functionals over convex regression classes in a fixed Gaussian experiment.
The many-period--many-control result gives conditions for synthetic-control factor-loading recovery under imperfect pre-treatment fit.
The proximal synthetic-control theorems identify treatment effects by using excluded control outcomes as predetermined proxies.

tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort average causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path. A maintained cross-date cohort-average transport restriction identifies it through the full historical wealth-path regression without event-date exchangeability. The raw generated-center local-polynomial estimator is exactly the event coefficient of an algebraic block-diagonal foldwise weighted least-squares panel regression on successful fits. Exact historical coordinates and an independently generated event center create treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, finite-spacing, and donor-modulus components. The smoothing term is present in the bookkeeping but never uniquely active; the sharp risk is the maximum of treated noise, path spacing, and \(N^{-\min\{\lambda,1\}}\) donor uncertainty. Matching lower bounds arise from joint panel laws on positive-probability query sets. A total retained-calendar-block interval combines observable Holder bias, separate exact Rademacher radii for calendar and event noise, and a fourth-moment donor-modulus allowance to attain the square-root expected-length frontier. Mean-only return-path information fails to identify compounded wealth by an explicit correlated-sign two-law witness, while the maintained full panel remains identifying.

project_justification.gap: Causal financial event-study theory treats mainly linear return contrasts, repeated-measurement regression fixes the query, generated-regressor theory moves every training coordinate, and synthetic-control intervals do not derive a generated-proxy minimax frontier for compounded wealth.
project_justification.niche: Many event studies observe historical proxy paths exactly, replicate untreated wealth blocks at each calendar window, and synthesize only the event-date query from donors. That architecture separates response replication, path-space resolution, and donor uncertainty without creating a classical inverse problem.
project_justification.fill: The project places finite-cohort identification under maintained cross-date average transport, an exact raw-estimator weighted-panel coefficient representation, estimation, conditional inference, and every least-favorable channel inside a single joint panel-law class. It derives the arbitrary-growth phase diagram, proves higher-smoothness donor saturation, and constructs a total covariance-aware local-polynomial interval with retained-block, event, and donor uncertainty calibrated separately.

related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and show why volatility mismatch makes buy-and-hold effects harder than linear cumulative returns; their result informs the maintained event-transport identification layer rather than serving as a theorem-level target. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates and a sparse-to-dense decomposition, while Gaiffas (2007) provides the pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) analyze generated coordinates attached to every training observation; Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) analyze replicated classical coordinate error requiring deconvolution. Those observation experiments inform the sigma-field distinction here. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest conditional synthetic-control uncertainty decomposition and beta-mixing block coupling. Chen and Christensen (2015) provide weak-dependence Gram-matrix control for higher-order sieve regression. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide the ordered-modulus language for honest expected length. Ferman (2021) supplies the many-period--many-control motivation for retaining arbitrary relative growth. Shi et al. (2026) identify synthetic controls through predetermined donor proxies but do not study generated-proxy minimax behavior.
technical_internal_limitation: The two-sided local modulus is maintained rather than derived for the whole Holder ball. It is non-vacuous for nonzero standardized gradients when \(\lambda>1\) and asymmetric cusps when \(0<\lambda\le1\), but flat surfaces lie outside the donor lower-bound subclass. Identification remains conditional on the maintained cross-date cohort-average event-transport equality; historical placebo stability can challenge it but cannot verify it at the treated event date. The mean-only nonidentification proposition concerns the restricted map \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\); the full historical wealth panel can distinguish its witness laws and remains identifying under event transport.
honest_scope: The order frontier, positive-probability joint-law embedding, exact raw-estimator FWL identity, finite-cohort DID reduction, higher-order moving-center stability, covariance feasibility, and conditional expected-length result are all to be proved. All identification, risk, and interval claims remain conditional on the maintained cohort-average event-transport equality. The \(N^{-\min\{\lambda,1\}}\) donor converse remains conditional on \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}, which is assumed rather than derived from the Holder ball. The field-tier contribution is the positive-probability joint causal-panel lower-bound embedding, exact raw-estimator FWL representation, higher-smoothness generated-center saturation, and feasible honest expected-length frontier. Smoothness adaptation and sharp phase-intersection constants are inherited future work from the banked predecessor and are not contributions of this proposal. The proposal does not claim event-date exchangeability, identification from mean-only return matching, growing \(S\), or growing \(p(H+1)\).

S2: Replicated-site random-design frontier with an independently generated evaluation center.
S4: Full-covariance calendar-block honest interval for the generated-center frontier.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, the potential-outcome setup, the bias decomposition around equations for abnormal-return, control-mean, and synthetic estimators, the buy-and-hold discussion, the proof of the identification proposition, and the Conclusion were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.opportunity: Lift a conditional generated-query experiment to a joint causal panel law and derive the identifying and FWL representations for compounded level wealth.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the linear return contrast in the anchor by the product map defining level wealth, then establish event-date transport for its conditional mean before any minimax reduction.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches joining buy-and-hold level wealth, local-polynomial generated centers, minimax rates, and honest intervals found no theorem with the four observation channels.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the anchor's synthetic-control consistency result after applying the continuous mapping theorem to compounded returns.
seed_details.rebuttal: A continuous mapping argument neither identifies the counterfactual joint return path nor controls volatility drag, random path-space holes, a root-\(N\) generated query, or uniform confidence length.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, the conditioning argument for repeated measurements, Theorems 1 and 2 on oracle and Holder rates, the lower-bound discussion, and the Conclusion were read from arXiv source version 2.
seed_details.opportunity: Determine the pointwise risk when \(T\) latent sites each carry \(n_s\) responses but the evaluation center comes from an independent donor experiment.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace integrated prediction loss by evaluation at one external random center and separate the site-spacing obstruction from the repeated-response empirical-process term.
seed_details.destination_search: Repeated-measurement regression and pointwise random-design searches found the two ingredients separately, not their generated-center product experiment.
seed_details.red_team: The answer is Yan, Yao, and Zhou's sparse-to-dense rate with \(N^{-\kappa}\) appended by a triangle inequality.
seed_details.rebuttal: That argument supplies no matching generated-center converse, no realized-spacing lower bound, and no proof that a moving local-polynomial Gram matrix adds no cross-term.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Section 4.2, Theorem 1, the definitions of the two smoothed first-stage terms, the opening proof decomposition, and the Conclusion were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the statistical boundary between a generated center and generated training coordinates.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Keep every training coordinate exact and perturb only the evaluation argument, so the anchor's smoothed rowwise first-stage remainder is replaced by a local modulus of the target functional.
seed_details.destination_search: Generated-regressor and errors-in-variables searches found no deficiency or rate-equivalence theorem comparing all four observation sigma-fields.
seed_details.red_team: The distinction is a verbal taxonomy, not a theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection defeats taxonomy as a headline; the surviving contribution is the factorization lemma and exact no-deconvolution phase boundary inside S1.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, independent and plug-in distributional approximations, the weak-dependence appendix theorem with its large-block--small-block construction, and the Conclusion were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a conditionally honest interval with estimated full donor covariance and overlapping beta-mixing calendar windows.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Linearize local-polynomial prediction scores around a fold-specific generated center before applying the anchor's conditional block coupling.
seed_details.destination_search: Synthetic-control prediction intervals and bias-aware nonparametric intervals do not combine generated-center modulus bias with replicated local smoothing.
seed_details.red_team: Condition on the donor sample and apply the anchor's dependent prediction theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Conditioning changes the target from \(m_s(z_{0s})\) to \(m_s(\bar Z_s)\) and does not control moving neighborhoods, covariance replacement, or honest expected length.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, the ordered-modulus definitions, the optimal one-sided and fixed-length interval theorems, the supporting-hyperplane construction, and the adaptation discussion were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.opportunity: Obtain exact expected-length constants at intersections of treated, smoothing, spacing, and donor phases.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed Gaussian regression operator by a product experiment with random design geometry, estimated covariance, and a nonregular generated-center coordinate.
seed_details.destination_search: Ordered-modulus searches found no exact-constant result for this product experiment.
seed_details.red_team: The constant follows by maximizing four known one-channel constants.
seed_details.rebuttal: At phase intersections the least-favorable chord can tilt across channels, so the product modulus need not equal the maximum of marginal constants.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, the weak-dependence matrix inequality, the spline and wavelet sup-norm rate theorem, the functional-normality results, and the concluding discussion were read from the arXiv source.

literature_map.settled: Repeated-measurement prediction rates, pointwise design adaptation, and multivariate local-polynomial bias--variance calculations are available.
literature_map.open_boundary: They fix or observe the query and do not combine replicated sites with an independently generated center and a causal transport layer.

literature_map.settled: Generated training regressors admit smoothed first-stage expansions, classical training error induces deconvolution, and estimated strongly convex minimizers can be sample-split from regression evaluation.
literature_map.open_boundary: An external Holder-irregular center has a first-order modulus phase distinct from all three.

literature_map.settled: Block coupling, weak-dependence Gram control, and bias-aware modulus intervals are established in separate fixed-query experiments.
literature_map.open_boundary: No result proves covariance-feasible conditional honesty and optimal expected length across every donor--calendar--replication ratio.

literature_map.open_boundary: Neither result supplies generated-proxy minimax rates for realized compounded wealth.
